origin.description: Count how many columns each string occupies in a fixed-width font.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

origin.details: Wide characters such as hanzi and emoji count as two columns. A precomposed u-umlaut and a u followed by a combining accent have the same width and different code-point lengths. Names on string are copied. NULL is an empty integer vector.
origin.value: An integer vector the same length as string.
origin.example:
x <- str_width(c("\u6c49\u5b57", "\U0001f60a"))
u <- str_width(c("\u00fc", "u\u0308"))
cat(paste0("str_width of hanzi and an emoji returns ", paste(x, collapse = ", "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_width of u-umlaut and u plus accent returns ", paste(u, collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Count display columns by calling stringi.stri_width.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector. A bare string has length 1.

translation.details: The width table is the one stringi uses, including the Unicode 16 additions checked against ICU. The result is always a list. Names on the input are copied when the lengths match.
translation.value: A list of ints the same length as string. A missing string is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.length import str_width
x = str_width(["\u6c49\u5b57", "\U0001f60a"])
u = str_width(["\u00fc", "u\u0308"])
print("str_width of hanzi and an emoji returns " + ", ".join(str(item) for item in x) + ".")
print("str_width of u-umlaut and u plus accent returns " + ", ".join(str(item) for item in u) + ".")
